title: Circles, Part 1: The Idea and an Easy Problem

beats.say: Circle questions ask for the circumference and area, the length of an arc or the area of a sector, and the measures of angles in circles.
They also ask for the equation of a circle in the coordinate plane. Angles may be given in degrees or in radians.

card.text: Equation of a circle; degrees or radians

beats.say: Every circle has a center, and every point on the circle is the same distance from the center. That distance is the radius.
A diameter is a segment through the center, with both ends on the circle. It's twice as long as the radius.
A chord is a segment with both ends on the circle. A diameter is the longest possible chord.
A sector is a slice of the circle between two radii, and the curved part of its edge is an arc.
A tangent line touches the circle at exactly one point. The radius drawn to that point is perpendicular to the tangent.
Everything about a circle comes from its radius. If you are given a diameter, an area, or a circumference, find the radius first.
An arc or a sector is a fraction of the whole circle. The fraction is the central angle over three hundred sixty degrees, or over two pi radians.
A central angle equals the measure of its arc. An inscribed angle, whose vertex is on the circle, is half of its intercepted arc.
The equation x minus h, squared, plus y minus k, squared, equals r squared describes a circle with center h comma k and radius r.
With degrees, the arc length is the fraction of the circle, theta over three hundred sixty, times the circumference, two pi r. With radians, it's simply r times theta.
With degrees, the sector area is the fraction times pi r squared. With radians, it's one half r squared theta. Never mix the two systems.
Easy example. A circle has a radius of nine. Find the length of the arc, and the area of the sector, cut off by an eighty degree central angle.

scenes.title: Easy: the fraction of the circle

beats.say: The arc and the sector are both a fraction of the whole circle. The fraction is the central angle, eighty, over three hundred sixty.
Eighty and three hundred sixty can both be divided by forty. So the fraction simplifies to two ninths.
The circumference is two pi r. With a radius of nine, that's two times nine times pi. We take two ninths of it.
Two pi times nine is eighteen pi. So the circumference is eighteen pi, and we take two ninths of that.
Two ninths of eighteen is four. So the arc length is four pi.
The area of the whole circle is pi r squared. With a radius of nine, we take two ninths of it.
Nine squared is eighty-one. So the area of the whole circle is eighty-one pi, and we take two ninths of that.
Two ninths of eighty-one is eighteen. So the sector area is eighteen pi.
As a check, convert eighty degrees to radians. Eighty times pi over one hundred eighty is four pi over nine. Then use r times theta.
The nines cancel. Nine times four pi over nine is four pi, which matches the arc length we found.
To recap. Find the radius first. An arc or a sector is a fraction of the circle, using the central angle over three hundred sixty.
Keep answers in terms of pi. Check using radians and r times theta.
